reference.title: Cable Lateral Raise
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the data sheet was not read)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you raise, breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s up, short pause, about 2 s down

prescription.load: Cable stack load is user-chosen; light: the arm is a long lever
prescription.progression: Add reps, then one plate on the stack; slower lowering

cues.text: Stand side-on to a low pulley on your left, feet hip width, knees soft. Hold the D-handle in the right hand in front of the hips, so the cable crosses in front of the body; left hand on the hip.
Breathe out and raise the arm out to the side, a little in front of the body, elbow soft, thumb forward.
Stop at about shoulder height; shoulder down, away from the ear.
Lower slowly in about 2 s back across the front of the hips; do not let the cable pull the arm down.
Brief pause with tension still on the cable, then repeat; switch arms after the set.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning away from the stack and swinging the handle up
mistakes.fix: Stand tall, brace the side of the trunk and lighten the stack.

mistakes.mistake: Shrugging the shoulder toward the ear
mistakes.fix: Reach the hand long and out; keep the shoulder blade down.
Stop at about 90 degrees; lateral raises above 90 degrees were linked to impingement signs (impingement study 2014).

mistakes.mistake: Bending the elbow more as the arm rises
mistakes.fix: Keep the same soft elbow from bottom to top.

kinematics.norm: From in front of the hips to about 90 degrees (the range used by Coratella 2020 for the dumbbell raise); raises above 90 degrees were associated with impingement signs (impingement study 2014)
Starts across the front of the body (the cable pulls the hand toward the stack) and finishes about 30 degrees in front of the frontal plane (scapular plane; clinical opinion)
Elbow soft, about 10-20 degrees, held nearly constant (clinical opinion)
The cable crosses in front of the body from the low pulley to the hand and keeps tension on the arm at the bottom, where a dumbbell gives almost none (clinical opinion)
Upright, no lean away from the stack (clinical opinion)
About 2 s up, a short pause, 2 s down (clinical opinion; Coratella 2020 used 2-0.5-2 with dumbbells)

sources.title: GymVisual, Cable Lateral Raise, video (movement reference)
Coratella et al. 2020, an electromyographic analysis of lateral raise variations and frontal raise in competitive bodybuilders (Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(17):6015)
Campos et al. 2020, different shoulder exercises affect the activation of deltoid portions in resistance-trained individuals (J Hum Kinet 75:5-14)
Characteristics of shoulder impingement in the recreational weight-training population (J Strength Cond Res 2014;28(4):1081-1089, PubMed 24077379)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the front or top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The cable load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with good form.
Return the handle to the pulley under control at the end of the set; do not let go with the stack lifted.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Pinching at the top: raise only to about 70-80 degrees and keep the arm a little further forward.
Balance: hold the cable tower with the free hand.
progressions: Lean-away cable lateral raise holding the tower.
Slower lowering (3 s) or a 2 s hold at the top.

muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Prime mover: abducts the arm against the cable. The lateral raise gave the highest medial deltoid activity among the tested exercises (Campos 2020, dumbbells); a neutral humerus (thumb forward) gave the most in the lifting phase (Coratella 2020).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Prime mover on the other side when you switch arms.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Helps, more so if the arm drifts forward or the thumb turns up (Coratella 2020).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Helps on the other side when you switch arms.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Assists abduction; the start across the body puts it under a little more stretch.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Assists on the other side when you switch arms.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Upward rotation of the shoulder blade; shrugging shifts work here.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Upward rotation on the other side when you switch arms.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Upward rotation of the shoulder blade as the arm rises.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Upward rotation on the other side when you switch arms.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff: keeps the ball of the shoulder centred.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Rotator cuff on the other side when you switch arms.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist the pull of the cable and the lean away from the stack.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist the pull of the cable and the lean away from the stack.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk still so the handle is not swung up.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Grip the D-handle on the other side when you switch arms.

phases.label: Handle in front of the hips

guides.label: From across the hips out to the side
